name: Coromandel International
title: Coromandel International Ltd - 506395 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 EBITDA fell 18% to INR944 crore on NPK margin squeeze and weak volumes; primary sales down 30% and production cut 15%, showing supply discipline, with management guiding to a better H2 on the new NBS rates.

summary.headline: Coromandel Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 18% YoY to INR944 crores on NPK margin compression, while revenue rose 6% to INR10,348 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was hit by deficit rainfall in key southern and western markets, rupee depreciation, high raw material prices and weak NPK offtake, with industry NPK volumes down about 40%. Consolidated revenue grew 6% to INR10,348 crores, helped by higher subsidy rates and NACL consolidation from August 2025, but EBITDA fell 18% to INR944 crores and PAT fell to INR523 crores from INR793 crores. Management deliberately cut primary fertilizer sales 30% to 10 lakh tons to protect working capital. Management said the Rabi NBS revision announced on November 17 and moderating raw material prices should lift H2, while stating it is only cautiously optimistic.

segments.name: Fertilizers (nutrients)
segments.commentary: Primary sales down 30% YoY to 10 lakh tons and consumption down 33%; production cut 15% to 7.7 lakh tons. Market share rose from 17% to 19% in H1. SSP volumes fell 13% to 1.9 lakh tons.

segments.name: Crop Protection (CPC standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22% in Q2, led by exports (exports growth 44%, above 40% of revenue). Standalone PBIT margin was 16% in Q2 and 17% in H1.

segments.name: NACL (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR374 crores, down 18%; EBITDA INR12 crores, sharply lower on high-cost inventory carryover and inability to pass on price cuts. Management called it a one-off aberration.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Described as a strong quarter; network expanded by 80 stores in Q2 to 1,300 stores, with a target of 2,000 in two years. Some white-label brands are expected to cross INR100 crores annual sales this year.

segments.name: Specialties, bio and organic
segments.commentary: Specialties growing at a sustainable 20-25%. Bio and organic fertilizers gained traction on high NPK prices; management said bio is a small share of revenue but carries much higher EBITDA margins.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 operating environment to be much better, with bounce back in production, sales and consumption, but said it is cautiously optimistic.
Management expects MRP moderation of at least 10-15% on NP grades such as 20:20 (bag price cited at INR2,100 vs INR1,350), subject to the detailed notification.
Kakinada granulation plant targeted for commissioning by February 2027, with full utilisation targeted for next Kharif.
Management said margins should come closer to earlier guidance from Q3 onward, but it declined to give FY27 EBITDA per ton before one more quarter.
Backward integration value gap expected to improve H2; management called a USD300-350 spread a safe assumption, and volumes at the Kakinada PA-SA plant to scale from October.
capex_capacity: Phosphoric acid and sulphuric acid plant at Kakinada (INR1,100 crores invested) was run at lower capacity until the Sulphur subsidy notification in August; now at full capacity.
Granulation plant at Kakinada expected to commission by February 2027.
A crop protection key-molecule capacity expansion is due to come on stream by end-November 2026.
Fluoro launch plant planned at Ankleshwar; a commercial plant could follow with capex of INR250-300 crores once customers are signed up.
Phos acid backward integration about 70%, with 20-30% headroom; management will keep some bought-out acid exposure.
demand_pricing: Industry NPK volumes fell about 40% in Q2; H1 industry NPK sales were 60 lakh tons vs 77 lakh tons, and DAP was flat at 44 lakh tons.
Management attributed the NPK slump to DAP being capped at INR1,350 per bag while NP grades such as 20:20 rose to INR2,100; the NPK:DAP mix shifted to about 30:70 from 60:40.
Channel inventory is estimated at 5-7% above last year; management said it is not high.
Sulphur prices are softening and may fall below USD900; phos acid rolled over at USD1,700 per ton; DAP prices broadly flat over the last two months.
Crop protection demand stayed soft in Q2 due to rainfall and weak agri prices; some customers deferred purchases and some molecules saw margin pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What MRP reduction is expected after the subsidy increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a minimum 10-15% moderation on NP grades such as 20:20, but the exact figure depends on the detailed notification. Ammonia prices are rising again, so timing remains uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: How much Sulphur subsidy was included in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: The subsidy applies to shipments above a USD800 floor price. Management curtailed purchases, and the subsidy helped August and September, but the amount was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-subsidy EBITDA rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty nutrients, retail, bio and SSP performed well; management also cited the ban on non-subsidy fertilizer sales in UP, Bihar and Maharashtra as a drag, and a molecule hit by carryover inventory in crop protection.

qa_highlights.question: Is the NACL inventory issue resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: High-cost inventory has come down and some raw materials were secured at better prices in Q2. Management said margin recovery at NACL may take several quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Kakinada granulation plant reach full utilisation next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets full utilisation next year, supported by retail and seed marketing in northern markets, with differentiated products such as boron- and zinc-fortified NPK.

risks_watch: Non-subsidy fertilizer sale ban in UP, Bihar and Maharashtra; resolution is needed to restore nano DAP and other non-subsidy volumes.
Quantum and timing of the MRP correction and whether NPK volumes recover in Rabi.
Rabi monsoon and El Nino outlook, plus Framework for Fertilizer Sale pilot challenges for NPK farmers.
NACL margin recovery and high-cost inventory unwind, with the EBITDA guidance still not provided.
Subsidy receivables of INR3,535 crores at September, and receipt timing.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management blamed external factors for Q2 and repeatedly said H2 should improve, but declined to give FY27 EBITDA-per-ton or quarterly numbers, saying one more quarter of visibility is needed.
key_quotes: Q2 was an unprecedentedly challenging quarter for the industry.
Revenue grew by 6% to INR10,348 crores; however, EBITDA declined 18%, mainly due to compression in NPK fertilizer margins during this quarter.
The challenge here is not the margin per se, but it is more of a volume.
Of course, I'm cautiously optimistic at this point of time.

adds.what: Fluoro launch plant at Ankleshwar (commercial plant possible, capex INR250-300 crores, contingent on customer sign-ups)
Retail network expansion to 2,000 stores in two years (from 1,300 stores)

growth.why: Management guides to a much better H2 with no explicit revenue growth number, citing the Rabi NBS revision, MRP moderation of 10-15% on NP grades, and Kakinada commissioning by February 2027; primary fertiliser volumes were cut 30% and it is only cautiously optimistic, so the outlook is flat to modestly positive and only partly backed by specifics.

oneOffs.what: NACL consolidation from August 2025 adds to consolidated total income growth; NACL standalone revenue INR374 crores, down 18%
Higher subsidy rates lifted revenue; subsidy share of revenue 81% in Q2 vs 83% last year, and subsidy share of profit 58% vs 72%

quality.why: Consolidated total income rose 6% to INR10,348 crores, helped by higher subsidy rates and NACL consolidation from August 2025, while EBITDA fell 18% to INR944 crores as NPK volumes dropped about 40% and primary fertilizer sales were cut 30%, so the headline revenue growth is not from the recurring core business.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said margins should come closer to earlier guidance from Q3 onward, backed by MRP moderation of at least 10-15% on NP grades such as 20:20 (bag price INR2,100 vs INR1,350), moderating raw material prices, and a USD300-350 backward integration spread assumed as safe; Q2 consolidated EBITDA was down 18% to INR944 crores.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kakinada granulation plant is targeted for commissioning by February 2027 (Q4 FY27), with full utilisation targeted for next Kharif, and a crop protection key-molecule expansion is due on stream by end-November 2026 (Q3 FY27).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects a bounce back in production, sales and consumption in H2, but primary fertiliser sales were cut 30% to 10 lakh tons in Q2, industry NPK volumes fell about 40%, and management is only cautiously optimistic.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fluoro commercial plant could follow with capex of INR250-300 crores once customers are signed up, and the Phos acid backward integration is at about 70% with 20-30% headroom, but no firm board decision was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give FY27 EBITDA per ton or quarterly numbers and H1 EBITDA fell 12% to INR1,705 crores, so no upgrade is signalled before one more quarter of visibility.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The H2 recovery depends on the MRP correction quantum and timing, the Rabi NPK volume recovery, and the monsoon and El Nino outlook; NACL EBITDA fell to INR12 crores and crop protection demand stayed soft in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fluoro launch plant at Ankleshwar is planned, and differentiated NPK products (boron- and zinc-fortified) are being pushed for northern markets, but no firm launch date was given.

rows.label: Non-subsidy fertiliser sale ban in UP, Bihar and Maharashtra
rows.why: The ban is a drag on non-subsidy volumes including nano DAP, and its resolution is needed to restore those volumes; timing was not given.

rows.label: Retail expansion to 2,000 stores
rows.why: Network grew by 80 stores in Q2 to 1,300, a 54% increase needed to reach the 2,000-store target, with some white-label brands expected to cross INR100 crores annual sales this year.

rows.label: Subsidy receivables collection
rows.why: Subsidy outstanding rose to INR3,535 crores in September from INR3,199 crores a year earlier, so receipt timing will drive working capital and deleveraging.

tone.note: Management was confident in the Kakinada plant, the Rabi NBS revision, retail and specialties, but cautious on the H2 bounce, declining to give FY27 EBITDA per ton; analysts pressed on the MRP correction quantum and timing, NACL recovery and the non-subsidy sale ban.
